po.en: Some speakers instead use {po} as a short form of {lo du'u} or {lo nu}. The terminator is {nei} or {tei}.

ce.en: Some speakers instead use {ce} to mean {ce'u}.

ki.en: Some speakers instead use {ki} to mean {ke'a}.

nei.en: Some speakers instead use {nei} as a terminator for clauses opened by {po} (see the note there.)

tau.en: Some speakers instead use {tau} to mean {tu'a}.

tei.en: Some speakers instead use {tei} as a terminator for clauses opened by {po} (see the note there.)

voi.en: Some speakers instead use {voi} to mean {poi'i}. For example, {ro voi mi djica ke'a} means "everything that I want".

a.en: Some speakers instead use {.a} to mean {.i pau}.

e.en: Some speakers instead use {.e} to mean {.i ji'a}.

o.en: Some speakers instead use {.o} to mean {.i ko'oi}.

u.en: Some speakers instead use {.u} to mean {.i ku'i}.

ua.en: Used more generally to express understanding or non-understanding.

e'i.en: Under a BPFK redefinition, this word *imposes* a constraint instead.

lo.en: This is “classic” {lo} as introduced in CLL. Modern interpretations and usage vary. In any case, {lo plise} means “(a/the) apple(s).”

le.en: This is “classic” {le} as introduced in CLL. Modern interpretations and usage vary. In any case, {le plise} means “the apple(s).”

loi.en: This is “classic” {loi} as introduced in CLL. Modern interpretations and usage vary. In any case, {loi plise} means “(a/the) apples.”

lei.en: This is “classic” {lei} as introduced in CLL. Modern interpretations and usage vary. In any case, {lei plise} means “the apples.”

banzu.en: Sometimes used as though it were defined as: $x_1$ is sufficiently $x_2$ for $x_3$ to happen ({raunzu}).

cinse.en: Often considered too broad, and used in a limited sense like: $x_1$ has sexual orientation $x_2$ (ka). See {jenri}.

dukse.en: Sometimes used as though it were defined as: $x_1$ is too $x_2$ for $x_3$ to happen ({du'enzu}).

moxna.en: Sometimes used as though it were defined as: $x_1$ is insufficiently $x_2$ for $x_3$ to happen ({mo'anzu}).

stagi.en: The $x_2$ specifies which portion of $x_3$ it is: lo najgenja cu stagi *lo genja* fi la'oi ly. Daucus carota .ly. = “carrots are the edible *roots* of Daucus carota.”

xruti.en: Sometimes used as though it were defined as: $x_1$ returns to earlier state $x_2$.
